why: The table already establishes that Direct Access has 'No authentication configuration' and 'no RBAC set,' but frames the consequence as merely 'not advisable if granular access is needed.' For a production-accountability audience that understates the finding: with no authentication, there is no identity to log against any action at all, which is a disqualifying fact for anything beyond a lab, not a granularity preference. This sharpens language the module already supports rather than adding a new claim.

If node egress to the image registry is blocked, every Kasten Pod sits in ImagePullBackOff with nothing earlier in the runbook having flagged the risk — that is a mid-install stall with no prior warning, which is exactly what this lens exists to catch.

loc: Lesson04_Maintaining_Veeam_Kasten_Over_Time.html · Section "Watching Veeam Kasten itself", Layer two: the built-in Prometheus instance — first PromQL code block
prop: Read it as: how many backup actions finished successfully in the last 24 hours. action_ended_total is the metric name; the curly braces filter to backup actions that succeeded; [24h] is the lookback window; increase counts how many happened inside it; sum and round collapse that down to one tidy number.
why: Every shell/Helm command elsewhere in this course gets a plain-English translation immediately after it — the Helm install caption literally says "read it as three sentences." The first PromQL query in this section (sum(round(increase(action_ended_total{action="backup",state="succeeded"}[24h])))) breaks that pattern: it gets no caption at all, and the second query only gets a one-line statement of its *purpose*, not its syntax. For a GUI-preferring learner with zero Prometheus background, this is a wall of unexplained syntax in a course that otherwise never leaves one — a confidence-curve break specific to this section. I could still follow the module's actual operational point (create the two recommended alerts) without decoding the query, but I couldn't have written a third alert myself. Note: PromQL syntax is generic Prometheus behavior, not a Kasten-specific claim, so this addition needs no product citation.
